title: Mixed Poisson models cannot give 70% probability to 108 of 153 NOAA hurricane count ranges from 2009 to 2025
abstract: We tested the model scope of a prior width explanation for NOAA seasonal hurricane outlooks. We derived an exact interval bound for every mixed Poisson count law and a sharp bound on the weight outside that family needed to reach a target. In a fixed published archive, 108 of 153 count ranges from 2009 to 2025 cannot reach 70% under any mixed Poisson law. Their median minimum outside weight is 13.82%. A finite-trial binomial test reaches the target with less dispersion, without changing endpoints. An exact counterexample with mean and variance both 10 puts 90.91% probability in 9-11 counts, whose Poisson maximum is 36.40%. Thus rate uncertainty cannot remove the family-specific limit, but variance equal to the mean does not establish an unavoidable count-noise floor. These are feasibility results, not fitted forecasts or a new calibration test. The study inherits range transcription and accrued counts and does not identify a physical error source.

display.caption: Model limits for fixed NOAA count ranges. The departure bound is per range, not an estimate of physical mixture weights. The equal-mean, equal-variance example shows that the Poisson bound is model dependent.
